managed-settings-keys.title: What managed settings control
managed-settings-keys.description: One managed-settings.json file groups supported keys into permissions, MCP servers, plugins and marketplaces, models, features and sandbox, and operational settings.

client-support-matrix.title: Which clients honor which keys
client-support-matrix.description: A matrix of eight managed-settings keys against Copilot CLI, VS Code, the Copilot app, cloud sandbox and Actions sessions, and JetBrains IDEs, highlighting unsupported combinations.

github-private-source.title: Publish from .github-private
github-private-source.description: Create an internal .github-private repository, add copilot/managed-settings.json, protect it with rulesets and code owners, fix any validation issues, then merge so supported clients apply the settings.

team-overrides.title: How team overrides resolve
team-overrides.description: An overridable enterprise default, a team mapping and a team file combine: mapped team members get the team value, which replaces the whole default, and everyone else keeps the enterprise default.

mdm-delivery.title: Deliver settings by MDM
mdm-delivery.description: An administrator authors policy values, the MDM service assigns them to a test device group, the client checks hourly without restarting, and the change is verified on a device before the assignment widens.

file-based-delivery.title: Deliver settings as a file
file-based-delivery.description: Write the settings file, place it with device management, and have users restart supported clients so the file loads at startup; until they restart, the previous policy stays loaded.

deployment-precedence.title: Which source wins
deployment-precedence.description: For replaceable keys, native MDM takes precedence over server-managed settings, which take precedence over a file-based settings file, which takes precedence over user and repository settings.

restrictive-composition.title: How restrictive keys compose
restrictive-composition.description: A matrix of six keys showing how values from several managed sources combine: unions for deny lists, intersections for allow lists, most restrictive for bypass mode, and whole-object replacement for telemetry.

endpoint-verification.title: Verify on an endpoint
endpoint-verification.description: Pick a test user and device, confirm a supported client version, refresh the policy, check that a test action is blocked, run a permitted action, and record the evidence; if not blocked, investigate the source, mapping and version.

drift-detection.title: Where drift appears
drift-detection.description: A timeline after a server-managed change: the change merges, online clients refresh within about an hour, an offline laptop keeps its earlier policy, an old client falls below the minimum version, and a reconciliation check tests sample endpoints.

change-review.title: Stage a settings change
change-review.description: A change lifecycle: propose by pull request, pass code owner review, validate, pilot with a mapped team, verify with a member and a non-member, change the default, then begin the next change.

rollback-plan.title: Roll back by delivery method
rollback-plan.description: Rollback lanes for server-managed, native MDM and file-based delivery, each with an action, a propagation time and a re-test, followed by a check that restrictive values from other sources still apply.
